Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{7}{3} & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{3}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{3} & \frac{5}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{5} & -\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{6}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{5} & -\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{5} & -\frac{2}{5} \\ -\frac{7}{5} & -\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$
